checks: Relative affine duplicates can be removed, and remaining ties lie in finitely many proper hyperplanes. If every complementary interior cell had constant parameter, continuity and connectedness would force constant L. Thus one relative-open cell contains a segment with strictly varying affine L.
On that segment s^(1+t) and s log s have strictly positive second derivatives for positive s and t>0. Adding any scalar multiple of the old affine restriction preserves the strict midpoint violation.

For any feasible concave path retaining the segment the old midpoint gap is zero. Dividing its new nonnegative gap by t would force the uniform first derivative to have nonnegative midpoint gap. This contradicts the reverse-power derivative on the same segment.

overlap.comparison: Describes sufficient feasible radial parameter jets on a positive neighborhood. The present segment proof rules out the reverse jet even for general concave paths with moving domains retaining the segment.

readability: The statement, sign conventions and scope are explicit.
review_method: Independent cold proof read followed by source, predecessor and exact arithmetic checks
summary: A varying affine cell contains a segment that rules out the reverse power and its uniform first jet by strict midpoint convexity.
